assets.name: The Free Firearm Sound Library
assets.role: weapons: matchlock report low layers, mechanisms (Free Firearm Sound Library, CC0)

license_evidence.page_statement: From The Free Firearm Sound Library homepage : The firearm sound library was the brainchild of a team of college students with a mutual passion for the audio and visual arts. In November, 2013 we launched a Kickstarter campaign to develop an extensive open source firearm sound effects library, and on December 7, 2013 our project was funded by an incredible group of backers and we went into full tilt production. This website serves to connect our backers with our two libraries, as well as to give credit to the backers who made it all possible. Along with the availability of these sounds comes the need to understand their proper application. The metadata included in the sound files along with some instructional videos will help make these sounds serve you to their full potential. Our team holds CC0 NO RIGHTS RESERVED for this library. It may be used without royalty or credit (though we would love to hear how you've used our sounds) for any application, personal or professional. Have at it! Please note that OGA is not affiliated with this project, and as such, we encourage you to visit their site so as to make sure you're getting the latest version of the files: http://freefirearmsfx.

assets.name: Park ambiences
assets.role: ambience: birds before rain, small river, wind (long field recordings)

license_evidence.page_statement: 3 recordings of ambience in different parts of a public park. One is close to a copse of trees, featuring birds chattering before the rain. The second is a recording of a small river with water falling over a low step, with some bird calls and frogs and other wildlife. The third is recorded in an open field with more intense wind. All recordings were made in a public park in Adelaide, South Australia, in winter. All files are recorded at 48kHz. To keep the filesize under 100mb, the two largest recordings have a bit depth of 16 bit. The park_ambience_wind file has a bit depth of 24 bit.

Four loopable rain SFX, with a length varying between 25 and 45 seconds. Recorded about two hours ago with a single mono mic at my window, then I processed it a bit, trying to make it sound stereo. It was more an experiment, but it can probably be useful anyway ;) Available in two formats, the samples are the same : - MP3, 192 kbps, constant bitrate - OGG, 160 kbps
